title: Petra and the Verdict
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Verity, founder of the cathedral town of Marrow's Reach, is exhumed for a disputed will, archivist Emrys Lockridge finds it empty—and a fresh ledger hidden in the crypt wall, written in a cipher only they can read. As the town prepares to try the dead man's estranged daughter, Sable Verity, for grave-robbing, Emrys discovers the ledger records a century of secret burials: people the town erased rather than mourned. Torn between loyalty to the cathedral that sheltered them and love for Sable, whom they once knew under another name, Emrys must choose between protecting the institution and exposing the truth. In the end, Emrys testifies at trial, the ledger is read aloud in court, and justice arrives outside the law: the town convicts its own founders' memory, Sable walks free, and Emrys finally claims a visible place beside her.
about_author: Juniper Vane is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing other people's secrets before turning them into fiction. They write mysteries about quiet people forced into loud rooms, and live near a cathedral whose crypt they have never been allowed to enter.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Emrys Lockridge catalogs the cathedral archive on the eve of the exhumation, establishing their invisible life among ledgers and relics. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: contentment built on deliberate self-erasure, shadowed by dread of what the open ground outside might yield.

chapters.title: An Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: At the exhumation, the town watches as Aldous Verity's coffin is opened before the magistrate—and contains only river stones and a child's shoe. POV: Emrys, observing from the crowd. Emotional beat: public shock curdling into suspicion, and Emrys's private horror that someone moved a body without disturbing the seals.

chapters.title: Sable Comes Home
chapters.summary: Aldous's estranged daughter Sable returns to face accusations of grave-robbing; Emrys recognizes her as Rowan, the runaway they loved and lost fifteen years ago. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: recognition as vertigo—the past arriving wearing a new name, duty and longing colliding in one glance.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Investigating the crypt alone, Emrys pries loose a loose memorial plaque and finds a coded ledger listing names, dates, and payments spanning a century. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: discovery as violation—someone trusted the archive to keep this secret, and now Emrys holds it.

chapters.title: Cipher of Saints
chapters.summary: Emrys works nights decoding the ledger, realizing the cipher keys off the cathedral's own liturgical calendar. The first decoded entries name paupers buried without rites. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: obsessive focus masking fear that every name decoded brings the trial closer to Sable's guilt.

chapters.title: The Dean's Quiet Warning
chapters.summary: Dean Halloway summons Emrys, gently reminding them that archives serve the church, not curiosity—and that testimony against the Verity family would embarrass everyone. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the cage made of kindness; belonging offered at the price of silence.

chapters.title: What the Stones Cost
chapters.summary: Emrys traces the river stones to the quarry where Aldous's fortune began, finding a mass grave marker disguised as a boundary wall. POV: alternating Emrys and Sable. Emotional beat: grief without names; two investigators circling the same wound from opposite sides.

chapters.title: Rowan, Remembered
chapters.summary: Sable confronts Emrys privately, demanding to know why they never searched for 'Rowan.' Old wounds reopen over candlelight in the archive. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: confession and accusation braided together—love resurfacing sharper for having been buried so long.

chapters.title: A Payment Every Michaelmas
chapters.summary: Decoded ledger pages reveal annual payments to the cathedral itself—hush money signed by successive deans, including Halloway's father. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding; the sanctuary was always bought and paid for.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Interest
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corven interviews Emrys as a material witness, probing their relationship with Sable and hinting the archive may be subpoenaed entire. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: exposure closing in from both directions—law and love each demanding the same surrender.

chapters.title: Fire in the Stacks
chapters.summary: A small fire damages the archive wing; the ledger survives because Emrys had hidden it, but the fire is clearly set. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve—someone inside the cathedral wants the past ash, and time is running out.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying sexton Bram Tull admits he helped bury the unrecorded dead and moved Aldous's body years ago at the old dean's order—but dies before naming where. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: mercy and frustration entwined; a good man's complicity explained, but not resolved.

chapters.title: Where Founders Sleep
chapters.summary: Following Bram's clues, Emrys deduces Aldous lies beneath his own statue in the market square, moved there to hide evidence of the quarry deaths. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grim triumph—the founder literally standing on his victims, in plain sight all along.

chapters.title: Halloway's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dean Halloway offers Emrys protection, promotion, and Sable's safety if the ledger disappears before trial. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive—everything Emrys ever wanted, priced exactly at their conscience.

chapters.title: The Night Before Trial
chapters.summary: Emrys and Sable spend the eve of trial transcribing the full ledger, mapping every name to living descendants in the town. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tenderness forged under deadline; love declared plainly because tomorrow one of them may be gone.

chapters.title: Theft in the Dark
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into the archive and steals the original ledger; Emrys's transcription copy is the last record left. Suspicion falls on Sable. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: despair and defiance—the frame tightening around her just as the truth becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Corven's Mistake
chapters.summary: Emrys catches Magistrate Corven burning ledger fragments, realizing he is Aldous's illegitimate grandson and has been steering the trial all along. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the law itself is a party to the cover-up.

chapters.title: Reading the Names
chapters.summary: At trial, when Sable is about to be convicted, Emrys takes the stand uninvited and begins reading the decoded names aloud until the courtroom refuses to let them stop. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: climax—terror transfigured into voice; invisibility abandoned mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Verdict Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The jury acquits Sable; Corven is arrested for evidence tampering; the crowd carries the ledger to the market square and demands the statue come down. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: catharsis—justice achieved not by the court but by the town hearing its own history spoken.

chapters.title: Under the Statue
chapters.summary: Workers lift the statue and find Aldous's remains along with quarry workers' effects; the dead are finally named and buried with rites. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: mourning completed at last—the archive's purpose fulfilled, not betrayed.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Chapter House
chapters.summary: Halloway resigns rather than face the chapter; he leaves Emrys the keys to the crypt and a letter admitting what his father did. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: sorrowful closure—institutions fall slowly, and forgiveness is a choice, not an absolution.

chapters.title: Petra and the Verdict
chapters.summary: Months later, Emrys opens the crypt to the public as a memorial, with Sable beside them; the final ledger entry, in Emrys's hand, records their own name at last. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging chosen rather than granted, love and duty reconciled in stone and ink.
